question: Why does causal self-attention reliably create an attention sink at position zero without depending on the [BOS] token's semantics, and can that mechanism be induced more efficiently during language-model pre-training without adding learned parameters?

key_findings.claim: The authors identify a two-block pathway in which causal masking first makes position zero structurally distinguishable and subsequent MLP computation turns that signal into a fixed-direction, high-norm representation that attracts attention.
key_findings.evidence: With [BOS] removed from LLaMA-3.1-8B, the position-zero state becomes directionally clustered before the second block's MLP and approaches cross-example cosine similarity near one after two blocks. Position zero alone must attend only to itself; other positions mix value vectors from increasingly many predecessors. PCA/t-SNE, exact removal of one layer-0 head contribution, layerwise norms, and cosine similarity jointly localize the proposed circuit, although they do not constitute a complete causal ablation of every circuit edge.

key_findings.claim: The paper's simplified value-aggregation model explains why causal position zero has a larger attention-output norm, but the result depends on idealized distributional and sparsity assumptions rather than proving the behavior for learned attention.
key_findings.evidence: For unit value vectors on a fixed-angle cone with pairwise expected cosine alpha squared, the expected squared norm of an attention-weighted sum is alpha squared plus (1 minus alpha squared) times the sum of squared attention weights. Causal masking fixes that sum at one for position zero; the authors assume it decreases with sequence length elsewhere because attention is sparse. Empirically, layer-0 attention-output norms fall from token 0 to token 64: 0.87 to 0.59 for LLaMA-3.1-8B, 1.04 to 0.87 for LLaMA-3.2-1B, and 1.37 to 1.05 for LLaMA-3.2-3B.

key_findings.claim: Removing [BOS] distinguishes a positional P0 mechanism in full-context LLaMA from an embedding-dependent sink in sliding-window Mistral.
key_findings.evidence: At threshold 0.3, LLaMA-3.1-8B without [BOS] has whole-network sink rate 89.40 versus 93.69 with [BOS], but Sink[2:] is essentially restored at 95.35 versus 95.39. Mistral-7B-v0.3 instead collapses from 87.45 with [BOS] to 1.87 without it. Repeating the first token eight times raises loss by 0.27 versus 0.21 in LLaMA-3.1-8B with versus without [BOS], but by 0.47 versus only 0.05 in Mistral, supporting architecture-dependent rather than universal [BOS] semantics.

key_findings.claim: TNLM Loss and Force-sink Masking implement complementary shortcuts to the learned circuit: one removes the position-zero prediction gradient, while the other enforces position-specific channel subspaces throughout the network.
key_findings.evidence: TNLM omits cross-entropy at [BOS], whose target is only the marginal distribution of the first content token, so P0 can act as a content-free register. Force-sink Masking retains k channels only at P0 and the complementary d-k channels only at other positions before every pre-norm, making P0 identification and semantic suppression structural. The principal runs use k=16, while the 100B-token Force-sink Masking+ runs use k=32 because k=16 was suboptimal.

key_findings.claim: At the 20B-token budget, both proposed interventions improve the six-task average over a parameter-matched Transformer at every tested peak learning rate, with gains broadly comparable to Gated Attention.
key_findings.evidence: At learning rates 3e-4, 4e-4, and 5e-4, Force-sink Masking scores 54.60, 55.35, and 55.94 versus baseline 52.26, 53.38, and 54.03, absolute gains of 2.34, 1.98, and 1.91 points. TNLM scores 53.93, 53.92, and 55.43, gains of 1.67, 0.55, and 1.40. Gated Attention gains 2.29, 1.98, and 1.94. Individual task behavior is less uniform: for example, TNLM at 4e-4 is below baseline on WinoGrande and both ARC-Challenge, while its overall mean remains positive.

key_findings.claim: The results show that large residual-stream outliers are not necessary for a strong P0 attention sink.
key_findings.evidence: Force-sink Masking yields substantially higher sink rates than the standard Transformer in Table 4 while Appendix C's layerwise plots show smaller position-zero hidden-state norms. The hard channel partition therefore decouples the attention sink from the learned large-magnitude suppression strategy, even though the ordinary circuit associates the two.

key_findings.claim: A sink is not strictly necessary for good language-model performance, so the experiments support a useful routing or rescaling function rather than necessity of the literal P0 pattern.
key_findings.evidence: Gated Attention has sink rates only 0.51 and 0.84 in the 3e-4 and 4e-4 runs yet improves the task average by 2.29 and 1.98 points. In the 100B-token runs its sink rate remains about 2.3 while its mean is essentially tied with baseline. Thus a gate can replace the sink's functional role, consistent with the paper's own framing but narrower than a claim that earlier P0 formation alone causes better performance.

key_findings.claim: Appendix E contradicts the prose claim that TNLM Loss and Force-sink Masking+ consistently outperform the baseline after 100B tokens.
key_findings.evidence: At checkpoints 200704, 202752, and 204800, baseline averages are 61.90, 61.43, and 61.58. TNLM is +0.23, +0.19, then -0.40; Force-sink Masking+ is +0.01, -0.07, then +0.33; ordinary Force-sink Masking is negative at all three (-0.51, -0.03, -0.45). Several combined variants are also negative. The appendix's literal 'consistently outperform' statement therefore does not hold for all reported checkpoints or named methods.

key_findings.claim: The observed association between earlier sink formation and higher downstream averages is correlational because each intervention changes the optimization problem as well as the sink trajectory.
key_findings.evidence: At 20B tokens, baseline sink formation is incomplete and the higher-sink Force-sink variants often perform better, but TNLM can improve while reducing aggregate sink rate and Gated Attention improves while nearly eliminating sinks. TNLM removes one loss term; Force-sink Masking removes shared channel capacity and imposes hard routing; Gated Attention adds learned nonlinear gating. No intervention independently changes sink onset while holding these other mechanisms fixed.

method.core_idea: Reverse-engineer the first two blocks of pre-norm causal LLMs to separate a structural position-zero identification signal from MLP amplification, then accelerate the same functional endpoint either by freeing [BOS] from next-token prediction or by enforcing disjoint residual-stream channel subspaces for P0 and all other positions.
method.mechanism: Causal masking makes P0's attention output an unmixed projection of itself, while later positions average multiple value vectors; the resulting norm and directional-consistency asymmetry is detected by early MLPs. MLP residual additions amplify a subset of P0 channels so the normalized direction becomes input-invariant and resistant to orthogonal gradient perturbations, allowing later heads to route otherwise unwanted attention to a stable semantic vacuum. TNLM Loss removes the cross-entropy term at [BOS]. Force-sink Masking applies m times h at P0 and (1-m) times h elsewhere before every layer's normalization, replacing learned position identification and outlier-based suppression with a fixed k-channel partition.
assumptions: The central circuit description applies to pre-norm causal decoders in which position zero remains visible; sliding-window and hybrid layers can use different mechanisms.

The value-vector cone model, unit-norm approximation, independence of off-axis components, and monotonic decrease of attention concentration with context length approximate learned activations well enough to explain the measured norm gap.
The first-order perturbation analysis treats generic gradient noise as approximately input-independent and small relative to the high-norm P0 state.
Sink Rate at fixed thresholds, measured over short sequences of up to 64 tokens, is a meaningful proxy for circuit completion and functional use.
The [BOS] prediction target is dispensable because only the loss on real continuation tokens matters for the evaluated language-modeling objective.

A fixed small channel count k can be selected without materially disadvantaging non-P0 representations, despite reducing their active hidden dimension and requiring retuning from k=16 to k=32 at larger data scale.
Parameter matching through larger FFNs controls enough of Gated Attention's extra capacity to make the downstream comparison informative, even though activation memory and forward computation differ.
Correlations between sink onset and downstream scores can motivate, but do not by themselves establish, a causal benefit from earlier literal P0 attention concentration.

techniques.role: Computes Sink epsilon over layers starting at a chosen depth so removal of [BOS] can be separated from later positional sink formation.
Uses layerwise norms, cross-input cosine similarity, PCA/t-SNE, and exact subtraction of individual head outputs to localize the early P0 signature.
Models value vectors with a shared direction and derives the dependence of attention-output norm on squared attention concentration.
Shows that a large residual norm attenuates orthogonal changes to the normalized P0 direction.
Drops the [BOS]-position cross-entropy term so its representation can specialize as a content-free attention register.
Hard-partitions residual channels between P0 and non-P0 tokens at every layer using a fixed binary mask.
Separates token-embedding semantics from the positional role by removing or repeating the first token across full-context and sliding-window models.

limitations: Author-stated: sliding-window and hybrid attention layers do not follow the same P0 behavior; detailed study of those mechanisms is left for future work.

Author-stated: there is no principled criterion for selecting the Force-sink channel count k; k=16 is chosen for the 20B-token runs and changed to k=32 after k=16 underperforms in the 100B-token setting.
Author-stated: the 20B-token baseline has not finished forming its sink, making that comparison potentially unfair; Appendix E attempts a 100B-token correction.
Author-stated: WikiText becomes anomalous under FineWeb-Edu pre-training and is removed from the main evaluation rather than explained.

Reviewer-identified: the mechanistic evidence is concentrated on a few LLaMA checkpoints and short 64-token inputs; the claimed two-block circuit is not tested by a complete causal intervention that selectively removes and restores its proposed edges.

Reviewer-identified: all from-scratch results use one 1B-class architecture family, one corpus, one seed listed in the setup, and six mostly commonsense or completion benchmarks; larger models, multiple seeds, long-context tasks, calibration, and generation quality are not evaluated.
Reviewer-identified: Force-sink Masking changes the forward computation and removes shared active dimensions, so 'no architectural changes' is too broad even though it adds no learned parameters.

Reviewer-identified: the methods do more than alter sink onset—TNLM changes the loss and Force-sink Masking changes representational capacity—so downstream gains do not identify early sink formation as the causal variable.
Reviewer-identified: Appendix E's downstream means contradict its statement of consistent improvement; effects at 100B tokens are small, checkpoint-dependent, and sometimes negative.
Reviewer-identified: memory overhead is shown only through representative plots and fewer-FLOP claims are not accompanied by a numerical throughput, wall-time, memory, or total-compute table.

Reviewer-identified: the current v2 incorporates the May 2026 Structural Origin paper after this paper's February 2026 v1; priority should therefore be assessed at the level of specific revision dates, not the current reference list alone.
failure_modes: If position zero leaves the receptive field, as in sliding-window attention, the positional circuit cannot provide a persistent global routing target and the model may depend on [BOS] semantics or another gate.

TNLM does not monotonically increase aggregate Sink Rate: at learning rate 4e-4 the sink appears only after layer 6 and its whole-network rate is lower than baseline despite a modest average-score gain.
A poorly chosen Force-sink width sacrifices too much non-P0 capacity or too little P0 capacity; k=16 fails to remain optimal at the larger data budget.

Hard partitioning every layer prevents any feature channel from being shared between P0 and content positions, which may be harmful for architectures or tasks that need semantic information at the first token.
Standard learned P0 circuits can produce massive activation outliers and attendant quantization or optimization difficulties even when the sink is functionally useful.
Sink Rate can obscure whether a sink starts only in deeper layers and can report a strong scalar pattern without demonstrating that the sink contributes useful values.
The FineWeb-Edu/WikiText mismatch can reverse the apparent progress of a commonly used perplexity benchmark.
At a data-saturated checkpoint, ordinary Force-sink Masking and TNLM can underperform the matched Transformer average despite very different sink strengths.
reusable_insights: Separate an always-visible token's positional role from its embedding semantics by combining token removal with layer-truncated metrics; whole-network averages can hide rapid recovery after the earliest blocks.
In a pre-norm network, direction and norm play different roles: norm can stabilize a direction against updates even though downstream sublayers consume the normalized direction.
Attention-weight concentration controls the variance and norm of value aggregation; causal receptive-field asymmetry can therefore create position identifiers without explicit positional semantics.
A learned outlier may be the network's expensive implementation of a simple structural partition or gate; replacing the function directly can remove the outlier while retaining routing behavior.
Loss terms at special tokens should be audited for whether they teach the intended sequence task or merely compete with a useful register role.
Evaluate mechanistic interventions after the baseline's emergent circuit has saturated; gains during circuit formation can disappear or reverse at a larger data budget.
Treat a literal attention sink and the functional ability to deactivate or rescale a head as distinct; learned gates can implement the latter without the former.
open_questions: Can selective activation patching or circuit editing remove the proposed two-block pathway and then restore the P0 sink and downstream behavior without changing the loss or model capacity?
Does the same causal-mask asymmetry induce an equivalent circuit in post-norm, parallel-block, mixture-of-experts, state-space hybrid, or sliding-window architectures?
What determines the optimal Force-sink subspace dimension as model width, data budget, context length, and modality scale?
Can a learned or randomized orthogonal subspace implement the same separation without permanently withholding k channels from every content token?
Is sink onset itself beneficial after controlling for training loss, active dimension, gating nonlinearity, parameter count, and compute?
How do TNLM and Force-sink Masking affect long-context retrieval, calibration, quantization, and free-form generation beyond the six reported tasks?
Why does FineWeb-Edu training worsen LM-Eval WikiText perplexity, and does that anomaly reveal contamination, tokenization, domain shift, or an evaluation bug?
Do multiple random seeds reproduce the small data-saturated differences in Appendix E?

competitive_landscape.title: When Attention Sink Emerges in Language Models: An Empirical View
competitive_landscape.relationship: direct prior on sink emergence, training dynamics, and the Sink Rate metric
competitive_landscape.difference: Gu et al. establish that sinks emerge with sufficient optimization, depend on loss and data distribution, behave like key biases, and disappear under non-normalized alternatives. The reviewed paper localizes an early two-block positional pathway, adds direction/norm analyses, and proposes two P0-specific training interventions.

competitive_landscape.title: Why do LLMs attend to the first token?
competitive_landscape.relationship: closest prior functional and theoretical explanation of first-token attention sinks
competitive_landscape.difference: Barbero et al. explain first-token attention as an anti-overmixing mechanism and study depth, context length, and packing. The reviewed paper instead claims a concrete causal-mask-to-attention-output-to-MLP circuit and distinguishes positional P0 from [BOS] embedding semantics.

competitive_landscape.title: Gated Attention for Large Language Models: Non-linearity, Sparsity, and Attention-Sink-Free
competitive_landscape.relationship: direct architectural baseline that replaces the sink's routing function
competitive_landscape.difference: Gated Attention adds a learned head-specific sigmoid gate after SDPA, improves training at much larger reported scale, and suppresses sinks. TNLM and Force-sink Masking add no learned parameters and intentionally facilitate or structurally instantiate a P0 register; their experiments show the functional role can exist with or without a literal sink.

competitive_landscape.title: A Unified View of Attention and Residual Sinks: Outlier-Driven Rescaling is Essential for Transformer Training
competitive_landscape.relationship: direct predecessor on the functional coupling of attention sinks, residual outliers, normalization, and gating
competitive_landscape.difference: Qiu et al. unify attention and residual sinks as outlier-driven rescaling and show that explicit gated rescaling can absorb their role. The reviewed paper narrows to why causal P0 is selected, models its value-aggregation asymmetry, and uses fixed channel partitioning to decouple a strong sink from large hidden-state outliers.

competitive_landscape.title: The Structural Origin of Attention Sink: Variance Discrepancy, Super Neurons, and Dimension Disparity
competitive_landscape.relationship: concurrent/follow-on mechanistic account incorporated by the reviewed paper's v2
competitive_landscape.difference: Li et al. provide controlled arbitrary-position interventions linking value-aggregation variance discrepancy, FFN super neurons, and dimension disparity, then use head-wise RMSNorm to restore positional parity. The reviewed paper's February v1 predates that record; its August v2 uses those findings but contributes a P0-specific two-block synthesis plus TNLM and hard channel masking. The overlap narrows any current-version claim to the exact circuit framing and interventions, not structural variance or FFN amplification generally.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The authors claim the first formalization of a two-block P0-Sink Circuit rooted purely in causal-attention structure, plus two parameter-free methods—TNLM Loss and Force-sink Masking—that accelerate sink formation and match Gated Attention without architectural changes.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper combines [BOS] removal/repetition across full-context and sliding-window models, early-layer activation localization, a cone model for value aggregation, a pre-norm perturbation argument, and 20B/100B-token pre-training. The two interventions are operationally distinct and the 20B-token table shows positive mean gains at all three learning rates.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The defensible novelty is the P0-specific composition of causal-mask asymmetry, early MLP directional amplification, and the particular TNLM/hard-subspace interventions. First-token anti-overmixing, sink-emergence dependence on training, outlier-driven rescaling, gate-based sink replacement, and value-aggregation/FFN variance amplification already appear in direct primary work; the latter is especially close and entered after v1 but before v2. Claims of causal downstream benefit and consistent data-saturated improvement should be narrowed because Gated Attention succeeds without sinks and Appendix E contains negative or negligible deltas. Force-sink Masking is parameter-free but is still a forward-architecture modification.

reviewer_notes: Read all 20 extracted pages end to end, including references on pages 10-11 and Appendices A-E on pages 12-20. Because the extracted multi-column tables on pages 9, 18, and 20 were interleaved, those PDF pages were independently inspected with Ghostscript's layout-preserving text renderer; Table 4 and Tables 10-12 values above follow the rendered PDF. Full-text coverage is 20/20 pages with no missing-text pages. Competitor discovery used at least three query families required by the protocol: (1) causal-mask/value-aggregation/MLP mechanisms for P0 sinks, (2) sink-emergence metrics, [BOS] ablations, training scale, and Gated Attention baselines, and (3) the paper's 'purely structural', 'parameter-free', and outlier-driven-rescaling novelty language plus cited predecessors. Official arXiv histories were checked on 2026-08-23. No earlier source found the exact combination of TNLM Loss and a fixed P0/content channel partition, but several sources already contain the main functional and mechanistic ingredients. This is a primary full-text review, not an independent second-reviewer verification pass.
